project.title: Persistence of spinach- and irrigation-associated microbiota through simulated gastrointestinal digestion
project.description: This study investigated whether microorganisms associated with raw spinach, including bacteria introduced from irrigation-associated surface runoff, can persist through simulated gastrointestinal digestion. Cut spinach was exposed to urban stormwater runoff, with some samples also inoculated with the foodborne pathogens Escherichia coli O157 and Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, then subjected to standardized in vitro oral, gastric and intestinal digestion with or without olive oil as a representative salad-dressing matrix. Microbial survival and community changes were assessed using culture-based enumeration and full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing. The study provides insight into how raw leafy greens may act as a route for dietary and environmental microbial exposure, and how digestion selectively filters produce-associated microbiomes and potential food-safety-relevant taxa.
